summary: Neighborhood gossip about Do-yoon, rumors at school, Grandma's family, the relatives, and a visit to a mountain temple.

scene.en: Sun-ja, have you heard about the young man next door? I hear he's rich — is that right?

scene.ko: 도윤이? 작은 회사 사장이야. 부자는 아니야.
scene.en: Do-yoon? He runs a small company. He's not rich.

scene.ko: 밤마다 하숙집 앞에 서 있다면서요? 별이 남자 친구였다면서요?

scene.ko: 아니요, 수염 없어요! 실제 나이도 젊어요.

notes.title: -다면서요?
notes.text: -다면서요? checks a piece of news you heard: 이사한다면서요? (I heard you're moving — right?). It's the gossip's favorite ending! Nouns take -(이)라면서요: 부자라면서요? 사모님 is a polite title for an older married woman.

notes.title: -다니!
notes.text: -다니 expresses surprise at news: 벌써 겨울이라니! (It's already winter?!) 그 사람이 유명하다니! (He's famous?!) 녀석 (rascal) is affectionate when adults say it about kids: 이 녀석! 성 = family name; Koreans say full names family name first: 김지우.

scene.ko: 할머니, 추석에 가족들이 다 와요?
scene.en: Grandma, does all your family come for Chuseok?

scene.ko: 그럼! 우리 집안 식구들이 다 와. 장남, 차남, 막내 딸… 며느리하고 사위도.
scene.en: Of course! My whole family comes. My eldest son, my second son, my youngest daughter… my daughters-in-law and my son-in-law too.

scene.ko: 자식이 세 명이에요?

notes.title: Family words
notes.text: 장남 = eldest son, 차남 = second son, 막내 = the youngest. 며느리 = daughter-in-law, 사위 = son-in-law. 외- marks the mother's side: 외할머니 (maternal grandmother), 외삼촌 (mother's brother). N(이)라도 means "at least, even just": 커피라도 마실래요? (Want a coffee at least?)

lessons.goal: Name aunts, uncles, cousins and in-laws.

scene.ko: 한국어 가족 이름은 너무 많아. 고모하고 이모는 뭐가 달라?
scene.en: There are so many Korean family words. What's the difference between 고모 and 이모?
b: to be many, to be a lot

scene.ko: 고모는 아빠의 누나나 여동생. 이모는 엄마의 언니나 여동생. 고모의 남편은 고모부야.
scene.en: 고모 is your dad's sister. 이모 is your mom's sister. 고모's husband is 고모부.
b: older sister (said by a boy or man)
older sister (said by a girl or woman)

scene.ko: 그럼 삼촌하고 외삼촌은?
scene.en: Then 삼촌 and 외삼촌?

scene.ko: 삼촌은 아빠의 남자 형제, 외삼촌은 엄마의 남자 형제. 그분들 아이는 내 사촌이야.
scene.en: 삼촌 is your dad's brother, 외삼촌 is your mom's brother. Their kids are your cousins.

scene.ko: 나는 누나하고 남매야. 누나 아이는 내 조카야. 진짜 귀여워!
scene.en: It's just me and my older sister. Her kid is my nephew. Super cute!
b: older sister (said by a boy or man)
older sister (said by a boy or man)

scene.ko: 우리 언니가 지난달에 결혼했어. 이제 형부가 생겼어!
scene.en: My older sister got married last month. Now I have a brother-in-law!
b: older sister (said by a girl or woman)
brother-in-law (older sister's husband, for a woman)
to come into being, to start; to get

scene.ko: 언니 시어머니, 시아버지는 어때?
scene.en: What are her mother-in-law and father-in-law like?
b: older sister (said by a girl or woman)
to be how (어때요? = how is it?)

scene.ko: 시부모님이 정말 친절하셔. 언니는 '아버님, 어머님'이라고 불러. 시어머니는 주부신데 요리를 정말 잘하셔.
scene.en: Her in-laws are really kind. My sister calls them "Father" and "Mother." Her mother-in-law is a homemaker and an amazing cook.
b: older sister (said by a girl or woman)

scene.ko: 친척이 정말 많네! 추석에 다 만나?
scene.en: So many relatives! Do you see them all at Chuseok?
b: to be many, to be a lot

scene.ko: 응. 그래서 추석은 바빠. 형제들, 사촌들, 다 와.
scene.en: Yeah. That's why Chuseok is so busy. Siblings, cousins — everyone comes.

notes.title: Calling relatives
notes.text: 고모 (dad's sister), 이모 (mom's sister — kids also call friendly women 이모, even restaurant ladies!), 삼촌 (dad's brother — also a friendly "uncle" for any young man), 외삼촌 (mom's brother). A married woman calls her husband's parents 어머님 and 아버님, and her older sister's husband 형부.

notes.title: Temples
notes.text: Korea has thousands of Buddhist temples (절), many tucked into mountainsides. Monks are addressed as 스님, and laywomen who visit are politely called 보살님. Many temples offer a "temple stay" (템플스테이) with meditation and temple food. 데려가다 = take someone along, 데려오다 = bring someone, 먹이다 = to feed.
